Definition: to hop, i.e. (figuratively) skip over (or spare); by implication, to hesitate; also (literally) to limp, to dance
BiblicalUsage: Pâçach is to pass over, to skip, to spare — and also to limp or halt between two opinions. The LORD passes over the houses marked with blood, He defends Jerusalem as birds flying, and Elijah asks Israel how long they will halt between two opinions.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Passover word is the gospel in one verb. God passes over the house covered by blood, and the same word warns me not to limp between the LORD and Baal.
RelatedEvents: The Passover; Elijah on Mount Carmel
